name: Yvresse
remarks: Launched 1993 as Champagne, renamed Yvresse after objections from the Champagne wine trade. NST review lists violet and cumin in the top; violet moved to heart, cumin dropped. Retail listings also cite peach, apricot, cinnamon, amber, benzoin. Current availability not verified.

name: Le Jardin de Monsieur Li
remarks: Fifth Hermès Jardin, March 2015, inspired by a Chinese garden. Published notes are a flat list: kumquat, jasmine, mint, sap. Hermès also cites sambac jasmine and bergamot. 'Green Notes' stands for sap; pale woods and watery jasmine come from the NST review.

name: Cristalle
remarks: Original 1974 EDT by Henri Robert. The 1993 EDP by Jacques Polge is a different, fruitier composition (mandarin, peach). Described here: the EDT.

name: Wanted Girl
perfumer: Fanny Bal, Jean-Christophe Hérault, Dominique Ropion, Loc Dong
remarks: Spring 2019, female counterpart to Wanted (2016). Ginger Lily = ginger flower. Some retailers list patchouli instead of vanilla in the base.

name: Lacoste Live
remarks: Marketed as L!VE, spring 2014, tied to the L!VE clothing line. Osmoz family: Aromatic Fresh. Retailers name Jean-Michel Duriez as perfumer but no brand confirmation found, so null. Only one top note published.

name: XS pour Homme
remarks: Some sources date it 1994. Mint is corn mint in the source. One retailer credits Michel Almairac; the Anthony/Mateu credit is more common.

name: Hugo Woman
remarks: 1997 EDT. Not to be confused with the 2015 Hugo Woman EDP (different formula). Longer retail lists add melon, peach, papaya, cassis, orris, amber.

name: Acqua di Giò pour Femme
remarks: Released 1995, a year before Acqua di Giò pour Homme, inspired by Pantelleria. 'Aquatic Notes' stands for Calone. Full list also has musk vodka accord, lily and rose.

name: Tsar
remarks: Source pyramid is longer (heart also jasmine, rose, pepper, lily of the valley; base also amber, coconut, musk, patchouli). Trimmed to 6 per tier.

name: Fleur de Rocaille
remarks: Singular 'Fleur' = the 1993 floral, distinct from Ernest Daltroff's Fleurs de Rocaille (1933). Pyramid from the Caron product page (EDP). Perfumer not published.

name: Jasmin des Anges
remarks: La Collection Privée Christian Dior, 2018, inspired by the Baie des Anges in Nice. Dior sells it as unisex (chunk hint said Feminine). Dior copy: sambac jasmine, apricot nectar, honey. Some retailers list the EDP as discontinued in their market.

name: Dior Addict Eau Fraîche
remarks: Name used for three formulas: 2004, 2012 (lotus, grapefruit, pomegranate) and 2014 (Demachy). Described here: the 2014 version currently sold. Official notes: Calabrian bergamot, freesia, lily of the valley, white musk; grapefruit and woody notes from retailer descriptions.

name: Valentina
remarks: Official name is Valentina (chunk name 'Valentina Donna'). Europe fall 2011, US 2012, face Freja Beha Erichsen. Truffle = white Alba truffle. Strawberry placed in heart per most listings.

name: Elixir des Merveilles
remarks: Official flat list: orange peel, caramel, biscuit accord (vanilla, tonka, milk), sandalwood, incense, Peru and Siam balsams, oak, patchouli, cedar, ambergris. Hermès page lists candied orange, benzoin, patchouli. Distinct formula from Eau des Merveilles (2004).

name: Byzance
remarks: Osmoz family Chypre Floral; other sources call it a spicy oriental. Rose = Turkish rose; anise also in heart. Existed in EDT and EDP; chunk merged on the EDP page. Reported discontinued by retailers.

name: La Vie est Belle Intensément
remarks: Sold as Eau de Parfum Intense, 2020. Lancôme copy also lists iris and vanilla bean in the base. Perfumers credited by one retailer as Anne Flipo and Nicolas Beaulieu; not confirmed, so null.

name: Yatagan
remarks: Caron calls it a 'flowerless' oriental chypre. NST gives a flat list; tiers distributed. Some retailers date it 1978.

name: Emporio Armani Diamonds
remarks: One retailer gives 2008. Cedar and patchouli placed in heart by some listings, base here.

name: Gaultier²
remarks: Near-linear amber, musk, vanilla; magnetised double bottle. Discontinued then reissued in 2022 (reissue listings cite jasmine and sandalwood, possibly a different formula).

name: La Vie est Belle Soleil Cristal
remarks: Summer edition 2021. Coconut placed in heart by the source, base by other retailers. Perfumer credits conflict (Ropion/Beaulieu vs Flipo/Ropion), so null. Lancôme US lists it as discontinued (seen in search result, not fetched).
